title: A significant model need not have every significant predictor
scenario_markdown: A chain models monthly sales with three predictors across 40 independent stores. ANOVA gives SSR=900, SSE=300, regression df=3 and residual df=36. Coefficient / standard-error pairs are advertising 4/1, store size 2/0.5, and sign age 0.2/1. Use alpha=0.05 for the overall F test and two-sided individual t tests.
assumptions: The model includes an intercept and three slopes.
Errors are independent, normal and have constant variance for the stated inference.
Each coefficient test holds the other included predictors constant.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is the overall F statistic? Select the value rounded to four decimal places.

options.hint_markdown: SSR/SSE is not F; first divide by their degrees of freedom.
Divide SSR by regression df as well as SSE by residual df.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is the two-sided p-value for sign age? Select the value rounded to four decimal places.

options.hint_markdown: The t statistic is not its p-value.
Alpha is chosen in advance; calculate the observed p-value.

stages.explanation_markdown: $t=0.2/1=0.2$ with df=36. Excel: `=T.DIST.2T(ABS(0.2),36)`. This p-value exceeds 0.05.

stages.prompt_markdown: How should the overall and sign-age tests be reported?

options.text_markdown: Reject the joint null that all three slopes are zero; do not reject the individual null for sign age conditional on the other predictors.
A significant F test proves all three slopes are nonzero.
options.hint_markdown: The overall alternative says at least one slope is nonzero.

options.text_markdown: The nonsignificant sign-age test invalidates the significant overall F test.
options.hint_markdown: The tests concern different null hypotheses.

stages.explanation_markdown: Overall F tests $H_0:\beta_1=\beta_2=\beta_3=0$ against at least one nonzero slope. The sign-age t test asks only about its partial coefficient. Sign age can be nonsignificant while advertising and store size make the model significant.
